attacks.attack: 1. Forge/tamper an item so it verifies
attacks.detail: (a) swap blob, keep commitment -> blob_intact=False (rejected=True); (b) forge matching commitment -> merkle_inclusion=False (rejected=True). Either path is rejected: you cannot keep the anchored commitment with forged bytes, and a forged commitment is not a leaf under the signed root.

attacks.attack: 2. Swap inclusion proof / index to another leaf
attacks.detail: (a) i's commitment + j's proof -> verifies=False; (b) i's proof claiming index j -> verifies=False. The audit path reconstructs a DIFFERENT root, so both are rejected.

attacks.attack: 3. Re-sign a forged root with a look-alike key
attacks.detail: (a) forged root signed by attacker, verified against the PINNED issuer key -> verifies=False (rejected). (b) attacker also swaps the shipped jwks to their own key -> verifies=True. ACCEPTED LIMIT: offline verification proves internal consistency + that SOME key signed it; the verifier MUST pin the issuer key out-of-band. A package whose own jwks is blindly trusted can be self-consistently forged — so the issuer key is distributed/pinned separately, not from the package.
